payload.title: tools/aria-acceptance/harness.py _read_cycle re-implements the 'runs of one cycle' read beside runtime_artifacts.read_runs_for_cycle because the owner has no read-only mode (its path helpers call ensure_tools_dir, which creates directories and rewrites integrity_index.json), leaving two readers of one fact
evidence: tools/aria-acceptance/harness.py:704-722 (_read_cycle: ensure_tools_dir_readonly plus read_runs_rows filtered by cycle_id)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/runtime_artifacts.py:289-303 (the owner: by-cycle file when present, else runs.jsonl filtered by cycle_id, both through ensure_tools_dir)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/tool_registry.py:328-354 (ensure_tools_dir mkdirs, prepares directories and calls update_tools_index)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/tool_registry.py:357-378 (ensure_tools_dir_readonly exists, but the owner does not use it)
payload.rule_violated: Single center, no duplicates: every concept has one owner and a second copy is deleted or pinned (user rule; CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach).
payload.notes: The harness's reader and the owner can disagree: the owner prefers the by-cycle summary file when it exists, the harness always reads runs.jsonl, and the owner cannot be called on a kept store without mutating it. A change to how a cycle's runs are selected (a new by-cycle layout, a status filter) lands in the owner and not in the exam, so the stamped baseline reads a different run set than the cycle phase reports, with no test tying the two. Close condition: Give read_runs_for_cycle a read-only mode (resolve paths through ensure_tools_dir_readonly, no index rewrite) and have _read_cycle call it; delete the private filter. Add a test that the exam and read_runs_for_cycle return the same rows for a store holding a by-cycle file and for one without. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
